A local copy is in `licenses/CC-BY-3.0-legalcode.html`.

The WAV recordings supplied in `assets/SalamanderGrandPianoV3_48khz24bit/48khz24bit/` are unmodified recordings from the original 48 kHz / 24-bit archive. The original README and both original SFZ files are preserved alongside them. The README's old V2 heading is preserved; its changelog includes V3, and the downloaded archive is explicitly V3. The retuned original SFZ credits Markus Fiedler; it is retained for provenance but is not used by this prototype.

NHIEN modifications (2026-10-11): new native bank manifest and independent SFZ mapping; velocity curve/crossfade; envelopes and pedal handling; synthetic resonance; EQ; generated room/reverb; limiting; MIDI performance and demo renders. No recordings have been claimed as recordings made by NHIEN. Demo matched copies additionally apply a documented static listening gain; MP3 previews are lossy encodings.

Suggested visible app credit (About / Sound Library, with clickable links):

> Piano recordings: Salamander Grand Piano V3 by Alexander Holm, licensed under CC BY 3.0. Source: archive.org/details/SalamanderGrandPianoV3. Playback, mapping and DSP modified by NHIEN.

Keep the title, creator credit, source link and license link with distributed samples and adapted renders. Keep this notice and original notices; do not imply endorsement by Alexander Holm. Do not impose additional restrictions on the CC-licensed recordings. Code is separately licensed under MIT (see LICENSE); the recording license is not replaced by the code license.

“CFX-style / Concert Natural” is an internal tonal direction only. This is a Yamaha C5 recording, with no Yamaha CFX recordings and no Yamaha endorsement. No commercial piano sample libraries are included.

App extensions (2026-10-11): voice-level sostenuto CC66 capture/release with sustain interaction, and attack velocity/filter modeling for soft pedal CC67. Source recordings remain unchanged. Sympathetic resonance (2026-10-14): each mode's drive is scaled below 1 kHz so low strings no longer lift a held note's fundamental by about 10 dB. Velocity layers (2026-10-14): each note plays the nearer of the two layers instead of summing both, since adjacent takes are 1-4 ms apart and comb-filter when mixed. Voices (2026-10-14): a re-struck key fades what it still sounds over 100 ms, and a near-full voice bank fades its quietest unheld voice over 20 ms, so voices are no longer cut (audible clicks).
